manual_scope.target: Reusable application-layer software for quantum-computing chemistry, machine learning, optimization, or finance, including their domain models, problem-to-quantum representations and algorithm workflows. Assess the main maintained implementation, not every possible downstream use.
manual_scope.non_software: Exclude repositories primarily containing documentation, tutorials, courses, resource lists, or example collections rather than reusable implementation code.
manual_scope.infrastructure: Repositories primarily implementing a language/compiler, runtime/provider, deployment infrastructure or simulator engine are outside focus. Adopted additional conditions explicitly include domain-specific simulator products. Mixed projects require functional review; names alone are insufficient.
manual_scope.classical_science: Exclude primarily classical scientific-computing packages that model quantum-mechanical systems but do not primarily implement quantum-computing application workflows. This is a domain boundary, not a programming-language filter.
manual_scope.other_quantum_domains: For this stricter four-domain proposal, standalone quantum-networking, hardware/error-correction and quantum-information-theory tools fall outside scope. These are substantive scope restrictions requiring explicit human confirmation, not universally unsuitable quantum software.
manual_scope.repository_granularity: Assess current independent application-module boundaries. A documented predecessor or component whose functionality was split or merged into retained repositories may be proposed for exclusion as a separate repository unit. This does not establish duplicate historical tasks; archive status alone is not an exclusion.
manual_scope.boundary_cases: Review mixed projects by their maintained functionality. Apply all adopted necessary conditions; application overlap cannot override a proven failure of another condition. Unknown or unaudited conditions remain unresolved.
manual_scope.instance_feasibility: For newly admitted samples, verify a feature Issue linked to its implementing PR and stable executable F2P/P2P tests under ../Build_Docker_WORKFLOW.md. Repository counts alone do not establish this.
manual_scope.unknown_evidence: Record not_audited or needs_review; never infer that no suitable Issue-PR pair or tests exist from missing audit evidence.
manual_scope.general_frameworks: Exclude primarily general quantum programming or training frameworks whose main maintained interfaces provide registers/circuits, generic quantum layers, differentiation, tensor integration or execution infrastructure. Judge the actual delivered functionality, not the word framework. A mixed project with independently maintained domain-problem models, problem-to-quantum mappings or application-level solving/prediction modules must be reviewed individually; examples alone do not establish such modules.
manual_scope.framework_comparison: TFQ PQC takes circuits/observables and emits expectation-value tensors as a Keras layer; propose E10 exclusion as a generic training framework. PennyLane also supplies a qchem Molecule API and molecular_hamiltonian mapping, with dedicated tests, so it remains a mixed project with explicit application modules. The distinction is functional and must not be generalized to excluding every quantum ML library.
manual_scope.research_experiment_collections: Proposed retrospective clarification: exclude repositories primarily organized as implementations and reproduction/extension pipelines for particular published experiments (including experiment-specific collection, calibration and analysis), even if they contain reusable helpers. Research use, publication, notebooks, or lack of PyPI distribution alone are not exclusions. General domain-problem libraries with reusable solver/model APIs remain individually assessed.
manual_scope.additional_conditions: Apply adopted_additional_necessary_conditions conjunctively. Passing application-module checks does not override an evidence-supported failure of any other adopted necessary condition.
manual_scope.primary_product_judgments: User confirmed excluding Qrisp as primarily high-level quantum programming/compilation infrastructure, and Qibo as primarily quantum simulation, execution and hardware-control infrastructure. Preserve their real application-module evidence. These are retrospective repository-scope judgments, not findings that those modules are absent.

functional_scope_confirmation.rule: User confirmed functional classification: exclude general frameworks; review mixed projects with explicit application modules individually.

decision_logic.rule: All applicable necessary conditions must be met. One evidence-supported failure is sufficient for exclusion; satisfying other conditions does not offset it.
decision_logic.scope: Use a consistent criterion and unit when evaluated. At explicit user request the existing seven are not re-evaluated in this turn; mark their compliance with new conditions not_checked, not pass.
decision_logic.unknown: Unknown, untested, or unaudited is not a failed condition.
decision_logic.new_conditions: The four additional conditions were adopted retrospectively on 2026-09-30 after user confirmation; they are not documented historical selection rules.
decision_logic.user_confirmation: User confirmed that failure of any one requirement is sufficient for exclusion.

adopted_additional_necessary_conditions.qubit_application_scope: The targeted application implementation must concern the qubit computing model; primarily continuous-variable photonic application repositories are outside this scope.
adopted_additional_necessary_conditions.python_native_application_implementation: The application core must be natively implemented in Python. A Python interoperability wrapper around application logic maintained in another language is insufficient. Native numerical dependencies alone are not disqualifying.
adopted_additional_necessary_conditions.not_a_domain_specific_simulator_product: Exclude a repository whose primary product is a domain-specific circuit simulation engine, even where supporting public domain representations and application-related operations are present. The mere presence of simulation functionality in a mixed project does not establish failure.
